description:
FOUND + FIXED s459am while diagnosing #814.  `p-str-x` computed string
repetition as `(apply #'concatenate 'string (make-list n :initial-element s))`,
i.e. it passed N ARGUMENTS to concatenate and consed an N-element list first.
MEASURED on SBCL's 2 MB default control stack: `'a' x 50000` fine, `'a' x
200000` dead with `Control stack exhausted` before any of the program's own
work ran.  On the 512 MB stack every PCL runner uses it survived, which is why
it had never been seen -- it took a runner that did NOT use PCLSbcl (#814,
tools/bench-exec.pl) to expose it.
FIX: one allocation, one pass -- `(make-string (* n len))` + `replace` per
copy.  Same result type ((simple-array character) either way), no list, no
argument spray, and O(1) stack.  `p-list-x` was checked and does NOT have the
shape (it uses `loop repeat n append`).
Bar met: gate PASS 191/6416, sweep GATE clean TOTAL 18340 (+0), companion op/
leg, Pl/t/foreach-raw-01.t + the existing string rows.
